hints: Look at the axes: $I$ is plotted vertically against $V$ horizontally, and the curve starts at the origin but bends over so its gradient gets smaller.
Recall that for an $I$-$V$ graph the gradient is $I/V = 1/R$, so a decreasing gradient means resistance $R = V/I$ is increasing with current.
Think about which listed component heats up significantly as $V$ and $I$ increase, causing metal ions to vibrate more and resist current more.
walkthrough: Identify the graph feature: $I$ on the vertical axis is plotted against $V$ on the horizontal axis, starting at $(0,0)$ and curving so the slope becomes less steep as $V$ increases.
State the physics rule: resistance is $R = V/I$, and on an $I$-$V$ graph $1/R = I/V$ is the gradient from the origin, so a falling gradient means $R$ is increasing.
Explain the cause: increasing $V$ drives a larger current $I$, increasing power $P = IV$ and heating the thin metal filament to a higher temperature.
Show the effect: higher temperature increases lattice vibration and electron collisions, so resistivity and resistance rise and extra voltage produces less extra current, giving the bend-over shape.
Rule out ohmic devices: constant resistance would give $I = (1/R)V$, a straight line through the origin, which does not match the curved shape.
Match the heating behaviour to the filament lamp. This is option A

options.A: The flattening $I$-$V$ curve shows resistance increasing with current due to heating of the filament.
options.B: A metallic conductor at constant temperature is ohmic, so its $I$-$V$ graph would be a straight line through the origin.
options.C: A resistor of fixed resistance obeys $V = IR$, so $I$ against $V$ would be a straight line of constant gradient $1/R$.
options.D: A semiconductor diode conducts sharply in one direction only after a threshold voltage, not a gradual curve from the origin in both senses.
